subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Tactics in Net/Wall, Striking/Fielding, and Target Activities
title: Concept model B: scoring systems and how they change optimal strategy
focus: scoring systems and how they change optimal strategy
essentialQuestion: How do you make an opponent or a target problem easier before you solve it?
privacySafeScenario: Build a tactical profile for one activity — strengths, tendencies, and the two adjustments most likely to improve results — then test it and revise.
studentTask: Learner applies scoring systems and how they change optimal strategy in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind scoring systems and how they change optimal strategy and name one adjustment for the next session.
completionCriteria: The learner completes or fully describes the scoring systems and how they change optimal strategy task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
adaptationChoices: Court size, target distance, implement, and object speed are learner-set. Seated, one-handed, and reduced-range versions are provided for every activity.
extensionChallenge: Apply scoring systems and how they change optimal strategy under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
